ports.name: timing_ok
ports.description: Timing checks allow selected request to issue

ports.name: bank_active
ports.description: Wrapper-provided per-bank row-open status used for row-hit detection

ports.name: bank_open_row
ports.description: Wrapper-provided open row per bank; four 10-bit rows indexed by request bank

ports.name: req_array
ports.description: DEPTH-entry request_t array from request queue

ports.name: req_valid
ports.description: Per-entry request-valid bits from request queue

ports.name: issue_valid
ports.description: Selected request is valid and should be retried until accepted

ports.name: issue_ref
ports.description: Refresh issue pulse gated by cmd_ready and timing_ok

ports.name: issue_txn
ports.description: Selected queue transaction issue pulse gated by cmd_ready and timing_ok

behavior.blocking_policy: lock selected index and hold it until issue_valid && cmd_ready && timing_ok succeeds
priority_rule: select the lowest-index row-hit request if any row-hit request exists
otherwise select the lowest-index valid request

implementation_constraints: compute row_hit[i] from req_valid[i], req_array[i].bank, req_array[i].row, bank_active, and bank_open_row
select the lowest-index row-hit request when any row-hit request exists
fallback to the lowest-index valid request when no row-hit request exists
scan queue entries in ascending index order
do not implement reordering beyond row-hit selection versus first-valid fallback
do not switch selected request while blocked
do not unlock or reselect merely because req_valid changes; lock clears only on successful_issue
do not remove queue entries in scheduler
do not use txn_valid or any direct transaction input as a bypass
all transaction issues must come from req_array plus req_valid
issue_ref must be gated by ref_req && cmd_ready && timing_ok
issue_ref and issue_txn must be mutually exclusive
when ref_req, issue_valid, cmd_ready, and timing_ok are all true, refresh has priority and issue_txn must be 0
refresh priority cycles must not create a new transaction lock
transaction lock acquisition requires !ref_req
candidate_success is candidate_valid && cmd_ready && timing_ok && !ref_req
candidate_blocked is candidate_valid && !ref_req && !candidate_success
new transaction lock acquisition requires candidate_blocked
do not create a transaction lock when the selected request issues immediately
issue_valid remains asserted for the selected valid entry while blocked
invariants: successful transaction issue is issue_valid && cmd_ready && timing_ok
row_hit[i] is true only when req_valid[i] is true, bank_active[req_array[i].bank] is true, and bank_open_row[req_array[i].bank] equals req_array[i].row
lowest row-hit index is selected when at least one row-hit request exists and no request is already locked
lowest valid index is selected when no row-hit request exists and no request is already locked
locked selection clears only after successful transaction issue
refresh issue is ref_req && cmd_ready && timing_ok
successful transaction issue is issue_valid && cmd_ready && timing_ok && !ref_req && !issue_ref
successful transaction issue must not assert in a refresh-priority cycle
if already locked and refresh arrives, the lock may remain but no transaction issue occurs until refresh is no longer winning arbitration
an unlocked selected request that issues immediately must not be retained as a stale lock
scheduler has no legacy transaction bypass path
scheduler never writes req_array or req_valid
issue_txn is a one-cycle successful-issue pulse for the selected queue entry
